ev.q: Voluntary Medical Male Circumcisions for HIV Prevention — 13 Countries in Eastern and Southern Africa, 2017–2021
Age was categorized as <15 years, 15–29 years, and ≥30 years.

equity.equity_measurement: Age-group shares of VMMCs are composition only; Rwanda and Tanzania are excluded from combined HIV testing estimates for 2020–2021.

notes: Design inferred: program monitoring with annual targets achieved and a recommended 80% follow-up threshold. Percent changes are arithmetic, not procedures; Stata is named but no tests or CIs are reported. The UNAIDS 90% access target is not assessed by the data.
view_issues: Text gives 43.8% of 2017–2019 VMMCs in clients aged 10–14 years, but the table's category is <15. Some table rows are inconsistent: Botswana 2021 age counts exceed the total, and Malawi total age percentages sum to more than 100%. The Discussion says device use fell to 1.1% in 2019 and 2020, while Results says it declined annually until 2020.
